paras: The attempted lynching of a Chinese man near Warm Springs, California, took place on the morning of May 25, 1888, when a group of people put a rope around the neck of an unnamed man accused of burglary and lifted him off the ground. The rancher whose house had been robbed got the man away alive and turned him over to a constable. A California Associated Press dispatch carried the story as a "Narrow Escape of a Chinese Thief From Being Lynched."

According to the dispatch, datelined Irvington by way of Niles, a man described as a "one-eyed Chinese burglar" entered the house of Mr. Henion at his ranch a mile or two below Warm Springs and was accused of taking $80. Henion's son saw him leaving and called his father, who overtook and searched him; the money was said to have been hidden in a barrel of water, where it was later found.

While Henion was placing the man under arrest, "a number of determined persons" were reported to have found a rope, put it around his neck and raised him several feet from the ground. Henion eventually got the man away alive and handed him to the constable, who locked him up.
The coverage does not name the man or those who hoisted him, and no report of arrests of the attackers, a hearing or a trial on the theft charge was found.

The only report found is the copyrighted California Associated Press dispatch printed on the front page of the Sacramento Daily Record-Union on May 26, 1888. Its headline and text called the man a "thief," a "burglar" and "the Chinaman," presenting the theft as established while giving the hanging only as something "it is reported" had happened. The dispatch offered no comment on the men with the rope and cast Henion as the one who saved the accused man and delivered him to the law.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of a Chinese man near Warm Springs, California
bases: A1 reports that 'a number of determined persons' put a rope around the accused man's neck and lifted him off the ground before he was rescued alive, an attempted lynching.

The man was hoisted by a rope over an accused burglary but was taken away alive and jailed (A1); no one was killed, so the episode is an attempted lynching, and the size of the group is given only as 'a number of determined persons' (A1).
Only one press dispatch, carried by the Sacramento Daily Record-Union (A1), was found, and it gives the hanging as 'it is reported'.

accounts.label: California Associated Press dispatch
accounts.gist: A one-eyed Chinese burglar stole $80 from Henion's ranch house; while Henion was arresting him, 'it is reported' that determined persons hoisted him by a rope, but Henion got him away alive to the constable.

framing.detail: The Record-Union ran the copyrighted California Associated Press dispatch under 'Narrow Escape of a Chinese Thief From Being Lynched', treating the man's guilt as fact and the hanging as hearsay.
